title: Supreme Court: Lorenzo v. SEC
summary: Dissemination of false or misleading statements with intent to defraud can fall within the scope of SEC Rules 10b–5(a) and (c), as well as the relevant statutory provisions, even if the disseminator cannot be held liable under Rule 10b–5(b). (No. 17-1077, opinion by Justice Breyer; 587 U.S. 71).

title: Supreme Court: Sturgeon v. Frost
summary: Alaska’s Nation River is not public land; and like all non-public lands and navigable waters within Alaska’s national parks, it is exempt under the Alaska National Interest Lands Conservation Act from the National Park Service’s ordinary regulatory authority. (No. 17-949, opinion by Justice Kagan; 587 U.S. 28).

title: Supreme Court: Republic of Sudan v. Harrison
summary: When civil process is served on a foreign state under the Foreign Sovereign Immunities Act of 1976, 28 U. S. C. §1608(a)(3) requires a mailing to be sent directly to the foreign minister’s office in the foreign state. (No. 16-1094, opinion by Justice Alito; 587 U.S. 1).

title: Supreme Court: Frank v. Gaos
summary: This class action settlement case is remanded for the courts below to address the plaintiffs’ standing in light of Spokeo, Inc. v. Robins, 578 U. S. ___. (No. 17-961, opinion by the Court (per curiam); 586 U.S. 485).

title: Supreme Court: Obduskey v. McCarthy & Holthus LLP
summary: A business engaged in no more than nonjudicial foreclosure proceedings is not a “debt collector” under the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act, except for the limited purpose of enforcing security interests under 15 U. S. C. §1692f(6). (No. 17-1307, opinion by Justice Breyer; 586 U.S. 466).

title: Supreme Court: Air & Liquid Systems Corp. v. DeVries
summary: In the maritime tort context, a product manufacturer has a duty to warn when its product requires incorporation of a part, the manufacturer knows or has reason to know that the integrated product is likely to be dangerous for its intended uses, and the manufacturer has no reason to believe that the product’s users will realize that danger. (No. 17-1104, opinion by Justice Kavanaugh; 586 U.S. 446).

title: Supreme Court: Nielsen v. Preap
summary: The Ninth Circuit’s judgments—that respondents, who are deportable for certain specified crimes, are not subject to 8 U. S. C. §1226(c)(2)’s mandatory-detention requirement because they were not arrested by immigration officials as soon as they were released from jail—are reversed, and the cases are remanded. (No. 16-1363, opinion by Justice Alito; 586 U.S. 392).

title: Supreme Court: Washington State Dept. of Licensing v. Cougar Den, Inc.
summary: The Supreme Court of Washington’s judgment—that the “right to travel” provision of the 1855 Treaty Between the United States and the Yakama Nation of Indians pre-empts the State’s fuel tax as applied to Cougar Den’s importation of fuel by public highway for sale within the reservation—is affirmed. (No. 16-1498, opinion by Justice Breyer; 586 U.S. 347).

title: Supreme Court: Rimini Street, Inc. v. Oracle USA, Inc.
summary: A federal district court’s discretion to award “full costs” to a party in copyright litigation pursuant to 17 U. S. C. §505 is limited to the six categories specified in the general costs statute codified at 28 U. S. C. §§1821 and 1920. (No. 17-1625, opinion by Justice Kavanaugh; 586 U.S. 334).

title: Supreme Court: BNSF R. Co. v. Loos
summary: A railroad’s payment to an employee for working time lost due to an on-the-job injury is taxable “compensation” under the Railroad Retirement Tax Act. (No. 17-1042, opinion by Justice Ginsburg; 586 U.S. 310).

title: Supreme Court: Fourth Estate Pub. Benefit Corp. v. Wall-Street.com
summary: Registration occurs, and a copyright claimant may commence an infringement suit, when the Copyright Office registers a copyright. (No. 17-571, opinion by Justice Ginsburg; 586 U.S. 296).
